facts.text: Mayfield’s name traces back to a gambler named Mayfield, kidnapped around 1817 at a racetrack near present‑day Hickman.
The Memphis, New Orleans, and Northern Railroad reached Mayfield in 1858, finally linking the town to the wider world.
In 1922, Lois Roach became the first female sheriff in the United States when she took over Mayfield’s sheriff’s office after her husband was murdered on duty.
Mayfield once housed the Woolen Mills and Merit Manufacturing Co., two of the nation’s largest factories for pants and suits.
The Graves County Public Library, located in Mayfield, serves as the town’s lending library and community hub.
Mayfield is the county seat of Graves County and was established as such in 1821, with the county formally organized two years later.
